name: Apache C++ Standard Library
listed_description: STDCXX, A collection of algorithms, containers, iterators, and other fundamental components.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The GitHub mirror (README, tests/ with no perf or bench directory, last commit 2012-09-15) has no benchmark data; stdcxx.apache.org, the Apache JIRA and the Apache wiki are blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED), and search snippets only say 'excellent runtime performance' without numbers. A snippet-only hint of an old stringstream test (gcc 3.2.3, 1.9GHz P4) had stdcxx slower than gcc.

name: APR
listed_description: Apache Portable Runtime; another library of cross-platform utility functions
reason: No numeric comparison found. README says only 'without sacrificing performance' and 'high performance allocators'; the mirror has no benchmark files and two rounds of web search for apr_palloc or apr_hash against malloc or std containers found no published numbers (pools are built on malloc and are documented for convenience, not raw speed).

name: argparse
listed_description: Command-line argument parsing library, inspired by Python's argparse module.
reason: No performance claim at all. README and FAQs describe usability against getopt; no benchmark, no numbers, no speed comparison anywhere in the repo.

name: bfish
listed_description: A single include ANSI-C Blowfish ECB crypto library. Public domain.
reason: No performance claim. README is an API reference only; repo has bfish.h, Makefile, example/ and test/ with no benchmark or speed comparison against OpenSSL or any other Blowfish implementation (Unlicense, 5 stars, 7 commits).

name: Bionic
listed_description: Google's standard library, developed for Android.
reason: No published numbers against glibc, musl or any external baseline. The repo has a benchmarks/ suite (with a bionic-benchmarks-glibc host target) and docs/native_allocator.md describes how to run allocator benchmarks, but neither contains results; the only numeric hint found by search (an omnirom mirror commit, memcpy 40.8% faster on A57 and 28.4% faster on A53) compares against bionic's own previous implementation, and that page could not be opened. Mirror archived 2023-11-08.
